title: Grade 4 Science — Tue, May 19
description: Food & Nutrition — Day 2 of 5: Food groups and the food plate
subject: science

questions.question: In which food group do you place milk and cheese?
questions.explanation: Milk, curd, cheese, and paneer belong to the Dairy group — excellent sources of calcium and protein.

questions.question: Rice, wheat, maize, and bread belong to which food group?
questions.explanation: Cereals and grains are carbohydrate-rich foods and form the base of most Indian meals.

questions.question: Which food group helps build and repair the body?
questions.explanation: Protein-rich foods (dal, egg, fish, chicken, soya) repair and build body cells.

questions.question: Fruits and vegetables are eaten for which nutrients?
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables are rich in vitamins, minerals, and dietary fibre. Eat at least 5 servings daily!

questions.question: Which food should be eaten in the SMALLEST amount according to the food plate?
questions.explanation: Fats, oils, and sugar are in the smallest portion of the plate — use sparingly. They are high-calorie with few other nutrients.

questions.question: Which food group should fill the LARGEST part of your plate?
questions.explanation: Cereals and grains (rice, roti, bread) provide the most energy and should be the largest portion.

questions.question: An Indian thali with dal, roti, sabzi, curd, and salad is an example of:
options: A balanced meal covering all food groups
questions.explanation: Dal (protein), roti (carbs), sabzi (vitamins), curd (dairy), salad (fibre) — a well-balanced meal!

questions.question: A meal of only rice and no vegetables, dal, or milk is:
options: An unbalanced meal missing proteins, vitamins, and dairy
Healthy if the rice portion is large
questions.explanation: Just rice gives carbohydrates only — missing proteins, vitamins, minerals, and dairy. An unbalanced meal.

questions.question: Which is a good source of iron (a mineral)?
questions.explanation: Spinach, methi, and other green leafy vegetables are iron-rich. Iron prevents anaemia (low red blood cell count).

questions.question: Which food is a good source of calcium?
questions.explanation: Milk, curd, paneer, and cheese are the best calcium sources for strong bones and teeth.

questions.question: Junk food (burgers, chips, cola) eaten regularly can cause:
questions.explanation: Junk food is high in fat, sugar, and salt — leading to obesity, tooth decay, and long-term heart disease.

questions.question: Which food gives energy AND some protein: eggs or sugar?
questions.explanation: Eggs are excellent — they provide protein AND fats. Sugar gives only empty calories with no nutrients.

questions.question: Why do children need more protein than adults?
options: They are growing rapidly and need tissue building
questions.explanation: Children grow rapidly — new cells, muscles, and tissues need protein. Adults mainly use protein for repair.

questions.question: Which vitamin is made by skin when exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Our skin makes Vitamin D when exposed to sunlight. That's why morning sun is recommended for children.

questions.question: A child who eats ONLY chips, cola, and sweets will likely:
options: Lack vitamins, minerals, and protein — risking health problems
questions.explanation: Such a diet lacks essential nutrients: no protein for growth, no vitamins/minerals for immunity and bones.
